question: Nawshad is a young social worker. One day, there arose a possibility of bloody clash between two groups of his village on the issue of the establishment of a library. Giving a balance verdict with prudent, he saved the villagers from an inevitable bloodshed. Because of his such contribution in social welfare, villagers elected him chairman of three village. At the inaugural speech, he advised them to appreciate the messages of historical speech of Prophet (Sm.) and also said, "That speech contains all round dictations for whole mankind"

[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is 'Charter of Madinah'?","marks":1,"answer":"Hazrat Muhammad (Sm) created a written document after consulting with the leaders of all tribes of Madinah and this written document is called The Charter of Madinah."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":""Conquest of Makkah is the shining example of Prophet (Sm.)’s forgiveness." Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"'Conquest of Makkah is the shining example of Prophet (Sm)'s forgiveness - this statement is relevant.
The Quraish of Makkah signed the Hudaibiyah Treaty with the Holy Prophet Muhammad (Sm) and the Muslims in the 6th Hijri year. On their violation of the treaty, Rasulullah (Sm) advanced toward Makkah with 10,000 followers in 630 AC. The Quraish were stuck with fear at the sight of the Muslim camp. They could not master courage to raise any resistance whatsoever. Muslim forces conquered Makkah without any bloodshed or opposition. After the conquest of Makkah, Rasul (Sm) forgave the people of Makkah who once tortured him in many ways. This is an example for the whole world."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Which side of Prophet (Sm.)’s ideal reflected in the role of Nawshad for establishing library? Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"In the case of Nawshad's role in establishing a library is a reflection of the life ideals of the Great Prophet's (Sm) neutrality and prudence.
Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was the greatest ruler of the world. He established good governance based on justice. He established peace and order in the society by conducting judicial work with discretion and impartiality. Which can be seen in Nawshad's activities.
Nawshad's work is similar to an incident during the Prophet's (Sm) youth. When the Holy Prophet (Sm) was 35 years old, the Kaaba Sharif was reconstructed. In that year there was a dispute between the various tribes of Arabia over the installation of Hajr-i-Aswad (Black stone). Every tribe wanted to get the credit of putting it in the right place but no tribe was ready to relax its claim. Consequently, a battle was about to start. At last, it was agreed that all will accept the decision of one who will first enter the Kaaba the next morning. It was found that the first to enter Kaaba the next morning was Hazrat Muhammad (Sm). All cried alike thus- 'Here comes Al-Ameen. We are confident of and satisfied with him. All accepted without dispute the solution offered by Hazrat Muhammad (Sm). He took off his cloak and placed the stone on it and the four leaders of the four clans held the corners of the cloak and he placed the stone in its proper place. This saved everyone from the inevitable bloodshed. So, it can be said that there is similarity in the role of Nawshad and Rasul (Sm)'s prudence and neutrality."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Determine the validity of the advice of Nawshad to the people.","marks":4,"answer":"The advice given by Nawshad to the people related to the speech of Rasul (Sm)'s farewell pilgrimage is valid.
Before taking his leave from the world, Prophet Muhammad (Sm) performed farewell pilgrimage. He gave a breakthrough speech during this time which is known as the speech of farewell pilgrimage. This speech has all the instruction for humans to lead a life. This matter is also observed in Nawshad's speech.
In the stem, Nawshad, after being elected as chairman, in his inaugural speech mentioned to the people about a historical speech of Rasul (Sm) and advised to contain the essence of it as this speech has the overall direction of the world humanity. This indicates the speech of farewell pilgrimage. Because the landmark speech given by the Holy Prophet to the sea of people present at the field of Arafat on the 9th of the month of Zilhaj in 632 AD is the Farewell Haji speech. There was all the instruction of world humanity. In this speech, Prophet Muhammad (Sm) ordered to develop friendly relations with all people and to forget hatred. He ordered everyone to be bound by the bonds of brotherhood. Through this speech of Hazrat Muhammad (Sm) along with establishing peace on earth, he pointed out the way to free people from the punishment of the afterlife. In addition, in this speech, the Holy Prophet (Sm) advised to treat the slaves, wives, and family members with respect and not to overdo it with religion. Through the ages, most people have found the right path from the speech of the Holy Prophet (Sm). In his Farewell Haji speech, he directed the people to establish a harmonious and peaceful society by being bound by the bonds of equality and brotherhood.
---"}]

question: Khatib of Baitul Mokarrom mosque’s said to musallies, "Be kind to wives, subordinates, do not exaggerate religion." He also said that our Madati Union Chairman Zahid saheb is in his council said. "you will follow me and help me as long as I follow Allah and His messenger".

[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"Who was Buhaira?","marks":1,"answer":"Buhaira was a priest during the Prophet's (Sm.) time. He prophesied about the Prophet (Sm.) being the Akihiri Nabi (Last Prophet) of the final phase."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"How was Mecca conquered? Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"The great Prophet (Sm.), along with ten thousand followers, advanced towards Makkah in the month of Ramadan on the 8th Hijri. Explain it.","marks":3,"answer":"The speech of Khatib Saheb is consistent with the epoch-making speech of Islam known as the farewell Hajj sermon.
In the tenth Hijri year, in 632 CE, the great Prophet (Sm.) performed Hajj in the company of more than 1 million Sahabis. As it was his last Hajj, it is known as the "Farewell Hajj". This contains adequate guidance on all issues pertaining to humanity. This guidance has been reflected in the speech of Khatib Saheb.
Khatib Saheb said, "Be kind to wives and subordinates; do not exaggerate religion." The great Prophet (Sm.) also said the same to warn mankind. We know our women are mothers. They are also creations of Allah. This is why wives have similar rights over men as men have over them. Hence, men have to behave decently with their wives. The great Prophet (Sm.) also advised to be very conscious of the subordinates. Their rights cannot be denied. He said, "Feed and dress them as you feed and dress yourselves. If any of them commits any unpardonable crime, set him or her free, but you shall not maltreat them. For they too are human beings identical to you, very much Allah's creation. All Muslims are brothers of one another, and you are tied to a common brotherhood." He also warned not to commit excess in matters of religion, as many preceding nations became extinct for that. Hence, the speech of Khatib Saheb is similar to the sermon of the Prophet's (Sm.) farewell Hajj."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze the teachings of Union Chairman Zahid saheb by identifying which caliph’s character his statement resembles.","marks":4,"answer":"The first Caliph Abu Bakr's (Ra.) character resembles the teachings of Union Chairman Zahid Saheb.
Hazrat Abu Bakr (Ra.) was the first to embrace Islam among adult Muslims. He was a dedicated servant of Islam. He was always engaged in the Prophet's (Sm.) service until his death, as well as Islam's service. He held onto the Quran and Sunnah as the best ideals of life. After the Prophet's (Sm.) death in 632 CE, he took on the responsibility of Khilafat. He took an oath on his election as Khalifah to follow Allah and His Rasul's (Sm.) guidance. This example has been reflected in Zahid Saheb's speech.
Chairman Zahid Saheb stated to the union, "You will follow me and help me as long as I follow Allah and His messenger." Likewise, the democratic-minded Hazrat Abu Bakr addressed the Muslim nation on his election as Khalifah: "You shall obey and follow me as long as I obey Allah and His Rasul (Sm.). And if I tread the wrong path, you will rectify me. Those poor among you are really strong to me as long as their rights are not restored. And those who are strong, they are weak before me till the share of the rightful claimants is not realized from them". Such a speech indicates obedience to Allah and His Messenger (Sm.) as well as democracy by giving importance to public opinions, etc. So, the exemplary ruler of all time, Hazrat Abu Bakr's (Ra.) characteristic, is nurtured by Chairman Zahid Saheb.
In conclusion, it can be said that Hazrat Abu Bakr (Ra.) is the ideal for all rulers. A part of his character has been revealed in the speech of Chairman Zahid Saheb.
---"}]

question: Rafiq read a book and learned that there was a time when women were not respected and valued in the society. They were tortured. There were disputes and quarrels in the society. And disputes were imposed unfairly. At such a time a stranger established an organization called 'Sabuj Sangha' to set peace in the area. As a result, disputes and quarrels in the society stopped.
parts:
[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is meant by Ideal of Life?","marks":1,"answer":"Activities of great man which are followed to make life perfect and successful are called ideals of life."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Why is Hazrat Abu Bakr (Ra.) called the savior of Islam? Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"Hazrat Abu Bakr (Ra.) is called the savior of Islam for his outstanding contribution to the service of Islam. After the death of the Prophet (Sm), Hazrat Abu Bakr (Ra.) very efficiently suppressed the renouncers of Islam and deniers of Zakat. Moreover, when many Hafez Quran became martyred in the battle of Yamama, there was a threat of extinction of the Holy Quran, he arranged to record the Holy Quran in the form of a book. Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"The description of Mr. Rafiq's book can be compared to the Arab society before the advent of the Holy Prophet which is known as Ayyam-i-Jahiliyah. Before the advent of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (Sm.), the people of Arab society forgot the teachings of the Nabis and Rasuls and indulged in anti-social activities. Their rites, rituals, conduct, and manners were barbarous and anti-humanity. This being the cause, the age has been called Ayyam-i-Jahiliyah, or the 'Age of Ignorance'. Women enjoyed no dignity in that society. They were thought to be objects of pleasure, as seen in the book read by Mr. Rafiq.
From the passage, it can be seen that Mr. Rafiq read a book and learned that there was a time when women had no respect or value in the society. They were tortured. There were social conflicts and quarrels all the time. And disputes were imposed unfairly. All these features existed in society before the arrival of the Great Prophet (Sm). At that time, they had no idea about a fair and beautiful social system. There was no security for people's lives, property, honor, or dignity. Manslaughter, burying daughters alive, gambling, etc. were common things at that time. Women enjoyed no dignity in that society. They were sold as slaves, and there were always quarrels. Therefore, it can be said that the description of the book read by Mr. Rafiq can be compared to the society of Ayyam-i-Jahiliyah."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":""The Sabuj Shanghai" established by the stranger is similar to which activity in the life of the Holy Prophet (Sm.)? Explain.","marks":4,"answer":"The establishment of 'Sabuj Sangha' by the newcomer is similar to Hilful Fuzul established by the Prophet (Sm). After seeing the horror of the war of Fiza, peace-loving Prophet Muhammad (Sm) was deeply and extremely disturbed. Thus, he formed Hilful Fuzul with other peace-loving youths, which is a peace organization. In its ideals, the Arab tribes of that time stopped quarreling and established peace and harmony. In the passage, the establishment of such an organization is mentioned.
It is seen in the passage that in the society of the book read by Rafiq, women were oppressed and there were constant quarrels in the society. A newcomer established an organization called Sabuj Sangha to establish peace. As a result, quarrels in society stopped. His work is similar to the establishment of Hilful Fuzul during Rasul's (Sm) youth. Because the Holy Prophet (Sm) formed Hilful Fuzul, or peace organization, with several objectives in mind. Such as serving the afflicted, resisting the oppressor, helping the oppressed, securing peace and order, maintaining peace among the tribes, etc.
Finally, it can be said that the organization named Sabuj Sangha, founded by the newcomer, is similar to Hilful Fuzul, established by Rasul (Sm), as its objective is to establish peace in society.
---"}]

question: Mr. Jasim is a teacher. One day he said in his classroom that there was a Khalifa in the history of Islam who embraced Islam at first among the adult Muslims. He spent all his resources in the battle of Tabuk. On the other hand, Mr. Kabir said that the Upazila Chairman does not discriminate in judgement. He also punished his son after the crime was proved.
parts:
[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is Hilful Fuzul?","marks":1,"answer":"Hilful Fuzul is a peace organization founded by Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Why Imam Abu Hanifa (R.) was famous?","marks":2,"answer":"Imam Abu Hanifa (R.) was famous for his contribution to Fiqh treatise or jurisprudence.
Imam Abu Hanifa (R.) was the inventor of Islamic jurisprudence. He formed the 'Fiqh Editing Board' consisting of forty of his students. This Board worked hard for twenty-two years to develop Fiqh as a complete book. Later he formed a special board with ten members from the forty board members. The contribution of this board is the most in the promotion and spread of jurisprudence. Whenever a Masahla (problem) came up, this board used to research it and gave a Fatwa (solution) after researching it in the light of Quran and Hadith. Thus, 83 thousand issues and solutions are recorded in Kuub-i-Hanafiya (Hanafi Treatises). Imam Abu Hanifa (R.) is famous for his outstanding contribution to jurisprudence."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Which Khalifah's ideal did the Upazila Chairman follow? Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"Chairman of Sadar Upazila followed the life style of Hazrat Umar (Ra.).
Hazrat Umar (Ra.), the second Khalifah of Islam, was the epitome of justice and fairness. He did not make any distinctions in establishing justice. There was a wonderful combination of hardness and tenderness in his character. As he used to be strict for truth and justice, he felt pain for the suffering of people. So, he tried his best to relieve their sorrow. He even punished his own son for drinking. Such lifestyle can be seen in the case of Sadar Upazila Chairman.
In the stem, the Sadar Upazila Chairman does not make any distinctions in the matter of judgment. He also punished his own son when he was found guilty in social justice. His work is similar to that of the second Khalifah of Islam, Umar (Ra.). He did not spare his son from punishment when he was accused of drinking alcohol. Hazrat Umar (Ra.) was a great example of justice, equality and humanity. So, it can be said that Sadar Upazila Chairman has followed the life ideology of Hazrat Umar (Ra.) and is fulfilling his duties accordingly."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Evaluate the contribution to Islam of the Khalifah indicated by Mr. Jasim.","marks":4,"answer":"Mr. Jasim referred to the first Khalifah of Islam, Hazrat Abu Bakr (Ra.) in the classroom.
Hazrat Abu Bakr (Ra.) was the first Khalifah of Islam. His rule is a model to follow for rulers of all times. Among the Khalifah in Islam, he was the first among the elderly men to accept Islam, and he spent all his wealth in the cause of Allah at the Battle of Tabuk.
Mr. Jasim, the teacher of the stem, told the class one day that among the Khalifah in Islam, there was one who was the first among the old men to accept Islam, and in the battle of Tabuk he spent all his wealth in the way of Allah. Which was the ideology of Hazrat Abu Bakr (Ra.). During the crisis of Islam, he dealt with all the disturbances of the state with a firm hand and discretion. He was also famous for his generosity. He gave all his wealth in the battle of Tabuk. After the death of the Prophet (PBUH), Hazrat Abu Bakr (Ra.) very efficiently suppressed the apostates and Zakat deniers and arranged for the Holy Quran to be recorded as books.
Finally, it can be said that Hazrat Abu Bakr (Ra.) was the savior of Islam. A ruler like him is a role-model for all kings and heads of state. So, we should also conduct governance with great determination and discretion like Hazrat Abu Bakr (Ra.) and work for the welfare of the country and nation.
---"}]

And representative Salam is cherishing the characteristics of Hazrat Abu Bakr (Ra.) who is the exemplary ruler of all time."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze the activities of the great man which are found expression in the deeds done by Kalam.","marks":4,"answer":"Kalam's activities reflect the equal humanity and the noble qualities of Hazrat Umar (Ra.).
The second Caliph of Islam, Hazrat Umar (Ra.) was an epitome of justice. He did not make any distinction between friend and foe in establishing justice. There was a wonderful combination of hardness and tenderness in his character. As he was strict for truth and justice, he felt pain for humanity. People's suffering tormented him. So, he made every effort to relieve their sorrow. Kamal followed this great ideal.
In the passage it is seen that as a public representative, Kamal believes in equality and humanity. He distributed the aid received from the government equally among the rich and the poor, friend and foe. Also, he wandered around the neighborhoods late at night to realize the suffering of the people. The same characteristic can be observed in the character of Hazrat Umar (Ra.). He was a democratic, humanist, and neutral ruler. He used to distribute the wealth received from BaytulMaaI equally among all. In this case, he did not do any distinction between the rich and the poor, and friend and foe. On the other hand, as a benevolent ruler, he used to roam about alleys and lanes in the cover of darkness to see for himself the conditions of the people. On hearing the cry of hungry children he personally carried flour to their house. He took along his wife to a nomad's tent to help a nomad woman in her childbirth.
In the end, it can be said that Hazrat Umar (Ra.) was a great example of equality and humanity. He has been exemplary in history as an ideal ruler by establishing accountable governance and ensuring the welfare of the people. Public representative Kalam has partially captured these ideals.
---"}]

[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"Who was Buhaira?","marks":1,"answer":"Bukhara was a priest who prophesied that the Prophet (PBUH) would be the last prophet."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Why is Ali (Ra.) called the gate of the city of knowledge?","marks":2,"answer":"Hazrat Ali (Ra.) is called the gate of the city of knowledge as he possessed extraordinary knowledge.

He was the greatest figure of his era in Hadith, Tafsir, Arabic literature and Arabic grammar. His poetry book 'Diwan-i-Ali' is an invaluable asset of Arabic literature. [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"Who was the father of Chemistry?","marks":1,"answer":"Jabir Ibn Hayyan is called the father of Chemistry."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Why is Abu Bakar (Ra.) called the saviour of Islam? Before writing each Hadith, he performed ablution and bath and prayed two rakaha of nafal. If the Hadith is considered pure through Istikhara, he would write that Hadith. Hadith scholars and Ulama have agreed that Bukhari Sharif is the purest book in the world after Al-Quran. 90 thousand students learned Hadith from Imam Bukhari (R.).
So, it can be said that Mr. Jamal discussed the biography of Imam Bukhari (R.)."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":""The type of ruler is obligatory for establishing the rule of law."— Analyze it in light of the scenario-2.","marks":4,"answer":"This type of ruler is obligatory for establishing the rule of law. Hazrat Umar (Ra.) was the epitome of justice and fairness. He did not discriminate in establishing justice. Everyone was equal to him. Even if the culprit was a close relative, he would not be spared from punishment. This is also noticeable in the description of the stimulus. In the stem, Anis studied the biography of Hazrat Umar (Ra.), the second Khalifah of Islam. Because, Hazrat Umar (Ra.) severely punished his son Abu Shahma for the crime of drinking. He died in this. Hazrat Umar (Ra.) was democratic. He used to consult the Sahabi on important affairs of the state and gave importance to their opinions. The humanitarian Hazrat Umar Faruq (Ra.) was a great example of equality and humanity. During Junua, he arranged for the public to complain against the ruler. In view of this, a man himself complained against him that no one had a complete shirt with the cloth obtained from Baytul Maal. But a full dress of that cloth is seen on the Khalifah. Where did Khalifah get extra clothes? On behalf of the Khalifah, his son Abdullah (Ra.) replied that I gave my share to my father, which included his entire garment.
From the above discussion, it can be said that Hazrat Umar (Ra.) was an embodiment of justice and fairness. Therefore, it is important to have a ruler like Hazrat Umar (Ra.) to establish the rule of law.

In addition to that he arranged for the expansion of the mosque which could not cope with the rise of the local people. parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is Sawm?","marks":1,"answer":"Sawm is to refrain from food, drink and sensual pleasure from dawn to dusk in order to please Allah."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"What is mean by avoidable knowledge? Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"By the activities of Mr. Rafee, the rights of employee have been violated. No man on earth can do all his work alone. Every individual has to look up to others to maintain himself. This is true for the relationship of employer and employee as well. The relationship between them should be empathetic and dutiful. It is absent in the actions of Mr. Rafee. Islam does not permit to differentiate between employer and employee, starting from food, clothing, and every kind of work. About the dignity and rights of the worker Rasulullah (Sm) said, “They (who work for you) are your brethren, Allah has made them subservient to you. It is proper that he (master) feeds them (servants) with what he himself eats, that he let them wear that what he wears and will not impose such burden upon them which they cannot carry out. In case it so happens, then he himself must come forward for their aid.” (Bukhari and Muslim). The Islamic regulation in respect of quick of wage is quite clear. Hazrat Muhammad (Sm) said- “Pay the worker his dues before his sweat dries out.” (Ibn Majah). Whereas in the actions of Mr. Rafi the opposite is seen. That is why with his actions he has neglected the rights of employee."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze the speech of Rabeya in the light of relevant Hadith.","marks":4,"answer":"According to the Hadith related to philanthropy and service to the created beings, Rabeya’s statement is relevant. Allah the Most High is the creator of everything. Except Himself, all the rest of that exist are creation or makhluk. As man is His creation, so are the insects and worms. Allah becomes satisfied when we show mercy on them. This is observed in Rabeya’s speech. In the stem, Rabeya’s speech shows the teachings of the hadith related philanthropy and service to created things. Allah is the Nourisher, Cherisher, Sustainer and Controller. He has not created all things in an identical mould. This is a test from Him. He has divided the creations in various groups and species, and maintains all for the benefit of mankind. Man is Ashraful Makhlukat or the best of creations. So, man should behave well with all the creations and practice good manners with all men. He should extend favours to beasts and birds. Allah the Most High becomes pleased if kindness is shown to them. Those who deal generously with all these creations are the beloved slaves of Allah the Most High. Allah loves them. In this matter Rasulullah (Sm) said: “All created beings constitute the Family of Allah. So, the dearest to Allah is that man who favours His created beings most.” (Baihaqi). So, it can be said that as human is the best of creation, it is must for human to show kindness to all the creation. That is why the statement of Rabeya according to the mentioned Hadith is correct.\n---"}]

subject: Islamic And Moral Studies
question: Mr. 'X' is an industrialist of Bangladesh. He is the owner of several industries. He is very aware of Namaz and Roza. But he insisted on paying the workers their due wages. When the matter came to the attention of the Imam of the central mosque, he said, "X’s work is against the principles of Islam." On the other hand, a student of Class eight named Saju while riding the bus to the city, saw one of his teachers standing there, he left his seat and let the teacher sit. The teacher was very happy and prayed fervently for his humble student.
parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is called student?","marks":1,"answer":"A student is someone who studies regularly and is eager to learn."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Explain the importance of Ilm in Islam.","marks":2,"answer":"The importance of Ilm is so immense that it has been made Farz for every Muslim by Islam."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Highlight the characteristics of an ideal student reflected in Saju in the light of textbook.","marks":3,"answer":"The act of respecting teachers by a student has been expressed in Saju. Notably, they always maintain a respectful, courteous, and exemplary demeanor with their teachers. Which is also noticeable in Saju. In the stem, Saju is a skilled student. He demonstrates this quality by offering the seat to the teacher while riding the bus. Such behavior exemplifies the ideal student. Other traits of an exemplary student include following teachers’ instructions, regular attendance in class, understanding the material thoroughly, abandoning the habit of pretending to understand when they don’t understand, and embracing the best education provided by teachers in all aspects of life. Like Saju we should develop ourselves as an indeed student."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"In the light of Imam Saheb’s comments, highlights the consequences of ‘X’ from the context of Quran and Hadith.","marks":4,"answer":"Mr. X has exploited the rights of laborers, hence he will face strong consequences in the afterlife. Islam has established proper rights for the laborers. One of these rights are paying them whenever its appropriate. Therefore, since ‘X’ denied the orders of Islam by not paying correctly to the laborers, he will face strong consequences in the afterlife.\n---"}]

parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is 'Mizan'?","marks":1,"answer":"The balance that Allah the Most High will install in the field of Hashr for measuring the deeds of man is called the Mizan."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"I have been given the right to 'Shafayat.' Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"The Prophet (Sm.) has stated the mentioned statement in order to describe his rights to Shafaat in the field of Hashr. The recommendation of the Prophets, Messengers, and other favourite servants of Allah for the welfare and forgiveness from Allah is called Shafaat. On the day of Qiyamah, the Messengers and Prophets and the virtuous servants of Allah will make recommendations. Allah the Most High will accept these recommendations and bless many men with paradise. However, the highest power of recommendation will be held by our beloved Prophet Hazrat Muhammad (Sm.). He himself said, \"I have been granted the right to make recommendations.\" (Sahih Al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim)"},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Identify Rahmatullah's performed Ibadat and explain its importance.","marks":3,"answer":"The Ibadat Rahmatullah has performed is Zakat. The importance of Zakat in Islam is immense. Zakat is the third pillar of Islam. Allah the Most High has made provision of Zakat to bridge the gap between the rich and the poor. If a person has Nisab amount of wealth, Zakat is Farz on him. In the Islamic viewpoint, Zakat is not mercy of the rich to the poor, rather it is the right of the poor. Zakat is one of the sources of Islamic economic system. The economic foundation and the success of the social welfare projects are dependent on it. It moves forward the flow of wealth and it teaches to reduce the wastage of wealth. The wealth of the rich reaches the poor also instead of remaining concentrated. As a result, the state economy takes off. Production increases and unemployment is reduced. The insolvent section of population gradually becomes solvent. The economic base of the state becomes firm. Zakat produces fear of Allah in the mind of man. Unless a Muslim pays up Zakat, he cannot continue to remain a perfect Muslim. Allah says: “Those who do not pay up Zakat, and they are not believers in Akhirat too.” (Ha-min As-Sajdah, Ayat: 7)"},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze the teachings of the worship that Imam saheb spoke about.","marks":4,"answer":"The Ibadat mentioned in Imam Saheb's speech refers to Sawm. It teaches how to stay away from immorality and understand the suffering of the poor. To refrain from food, drink, and sensual pleasure from dawn to dusk in order to please Allah is known as Sawm. It is one of the five pillars of Islam. Imam Saheb has indicated this Ibadat in his speech. Imam Saheb has said that there is an Ibadat that keeps man away from greed, lust, violence, hatred, and anger. This is true for Sawm. It has unlimited lessons for us. Sawm is like a shield. Man does not eat or drink anything in spite of the pain of hunger and thirst and does not enjoy sensual pleasure for the sake of love and fear of Allah. As a result, man learns to stay away from immoral deeds. He does not fall for greed and avarice, envy and hatred, anger and agitation, etc. In addition, mutual sympathy and fellow feeling are developed by the cultivation of Sawm. The Holy Prophet (Sm.) said, \"This month is the month of sympathy.\" A man practicing Sawm can imagine how distressing the pain of hunger and thirst can be. At this point, feelings of sympathy and fellow-feeling are developed towards hungry people. Therefore, from the discussion, it can be understood that Imam Saheb has explained the matter of Sawm. We can learn moral and social lessons through Sawm. Simply put, Sawm encourages us to stay away from immorality and follow Allah's laws.\n---"}]

question: According to Islamic Shariah, Mr. Zayed pays a specific portion of his wealth to some specific heads every year. On the other hand his friends, Mr. Rashed, performs an Ibadat every year by which he can feel the suffering of the poor and the destitute of society.

Salat keeps a Mu’min away from harmful and indecent actions. Those who perform Salat guard themselves against falsehood and inappropriate behavior in order to keep them pure and sacred.Five-time prayers daily lead to the forgiveness of sins. Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"The fundamental Ibadat in Islam performed by Mr. Zayed is Zakat. In the Islamic Shariat point of view, the spending of 2.50 percent of a Muslim owner having Nisab (taxable) amount of wealth at the close of the year on specified heads of expenditure is termed as Zakat. Zakat is a Farz Ibadat. Allah has provisioned for Zakat in Islam with a view to bridging the gap between the poor and the rich. It is one of the five pillars of Islam. The activities of Mr. Zayed, paying a specific portion of his wealth to specific heads every year, align perfectly with this definition and purpose of Zakat."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"“The social importance of Mr. Rashed's Ibadat is immense.” — Present you arguments for this statement.","marks":4,"answer":"‘The Ibadat Sawm performed by Mr. Rashed has immense importance in the society’— I agree with this statement. From a religious perspective the significance of Sawm is immense. Allah increases the rewards of all noble deeds from ten to seven hundred folds in the month of Ramadan. Sawm is observed in a fixed month which is Ramadan. During this month Allah increases the rewards of every noble deeds from ten to seven hundred folds. As Sawm is observed for Allah with the hope of return, Allah the Most High forgives all previous sins of Sayim. As the holy Prophet (Sm) has said: \"Allah the Most High forgives all the past sins of a person who observes fast by cherishing faith in and hope of reward from Allah.\" (Bukhari) Socially, Sawm teaches empathy and compassion. By experiencing hunger and thirst, a fasting person can better understand the plight of the poor and needy. This fosters a sense of social responsibility and encourages charity (Sadaqah) and Zakat. It promotes self-discipline, patience, and control over desires, which are essential for a harmonious society. The collective observance of Sawm during Ramadan strengthens community bonds through shared experiences, nightly prayers (Taraweeh), and breaking fast together (Iftar). Therefore, the social importance of Sawm, as performed by Mr. Rashed, is indeed immense."}]

The etymological meaning of the word Zakat is holiness, purity and increase.In the Islamic Shariat point of view, the spending of 2.50 percent of a Muslim owner having Nisab (taxable) amount of wealth at the close of the year on specific heads of expenditure is termed as Zakat.The activities of Nafis as mentioned in the stem have been quite the opposite to the idea of Zakat. According to the information given in the stem, Nafis is a rich man. He offers his Salat regularly and also had performed Haji in last year. But at the end of the year, he does not pay Allah's prescribed portion of his wealth to certain sectors. It indicates that he did not pay up his Zakat. Not paying up Zakat or not giving importance to it is equivalent to Kufr. Zakat is a Farz Ibadat. It is not optional; just like other Farz Ibadat such as Salat, Sawm, Haji etc, Zakat is also Farz. In many places of the holy Quran, Allah has ordered to pay up Zakat as well as praying Salat. Allah said, \"Establish your prayer and pay up your Zakat\". (Sura: An-Noor, Ayat: 56). But in the stem, Nafis disobeyed this order by not paying up Zakat.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"Analyze the accuracy of the statement of Rafiq's father.","marks":4,"answer":"The statement given by Rafiq's father regarding the religious importance of Salat is accurate. Salat is an Arabic word. It means prayer, asking for forgiveness and blessing. Since we are Allah's slaves and we pray to the Almighty Allah and ask for mercy and forgiveness through Salat, hence it is named so. The religious importance of Salat is immense. It brings a person closer to Allah, strengthens Iman, and helps purify his soul. All these had been reflected in the statement given by Rafiq's father. According to the stem, as soon as Rafiq hears Azan, he puts aside all his work and prepares for performing a special Ibadat and completes it. This Ibadat is Salat. In this regard, his father said that, \"It helps man to gain Allah's nearness\". In a Muslim's daily life, the importance of Salat is unparalleled. Salat assists a person in attaining closeness to Allah. Through it, faith becomes stronger, and the soul becomes purified. Salat encourages a person to wake up early from sleep, which is highly beneficial for health. The Prophet (Sm.) said about the significance of Salat, \"One who offers Salat with attention, that Salat will be Noor for him\". (Tabarani). Based on the discussion above, Rafiq's father has rightly emphasized the importance of Salat. Therefore, it is essential for each of us to perform Salat correctly and at the appropriate times.","image":null,"image_url":null}]

parts: [{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"What is the aim of the creation of human being?","marks":1,"answer":"The aim of the creation of human being is to worship Allah.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"Explain the relationship between the education and morality.","marks":2,"answer":"To live an idealistic life, education and morality are deeply connected to each other. Education teaches people to apply accumulated knowledge and experience successfully in their life. If there is a combination of morality and ethics in this education, then people can be good idealists. An idea of morality teachpeople to move, stand, sit, behave, conduct, transaction everything ethically. He cannot do his ways by unethical means in family, society or even in his country or state. This is how education and morality are deeply related.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"What type of Ibadat Mr. 'X' is refrain from? Explain","marks":3,"answer":"Mr. 'X' in refrain from performing Haqqul Ibad. Ibadat is of two types, one of which is Haqqul Ibad. It is the haqq or rights of fellow slaves of Allah. Islam has strictly ordered ensure these haqq. Mr. 'X' has disobeyed this order. Mr. 'X' did not help his neighbours, also he did not visit his sick sister. But we live in a society with our parents, siblings, relatives, neighbours and we share bonding with them. In this case, our duty is to help each other in distress. This mutual sympathy and responsibility is known as Haqqul Ibad in Islam. Prophet Rasul (Sm.) has said that, \"Verily your Rabb (Nourisher), your own body, your wife and children have got rights upon you”. In another place, Rasulullah (Sm.) further said, “A Muslim has got six rights upon another fellow Muslim. These are to return his salvation (Salam), to visit a patient, to attend his Janaza, to accept his invitation, to help one who is oppressed, and to respond to his sneezing” (Bukhari and Muslim). So it can be said that Mr. ‘X’ abstained from performing Haqqul Ibad.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"Are you agree with comments of Jiku's mother? Give the logics in favour of your opinion.","marks":4,"answer":"Since the importance of morality has been emphasized, I agree with Jiku’s mother. Education helps humans become true humans. It liberates the human heart from the darkness of ignorance and illuminates it with the light of knowledge. Without it, humans descend to the level of lawless animals. The support for this idea is evident in the words of Jiku’s mother. She holds the lack of proper education responsible for her son’s downfall. Her statement is reasonable. When education is accompanied by moral values, it is considered true education. Such education nurtures fundamental human qualities. It enables individuals to discern between good and bad. Traits like honesty, integrity, kindness, and sweet words are instilled through this type of education. Such individuals never waste time unnecessarily or mix with the wrong crowd. On the contrary, due to education devoid of ethics and character, humans become inferior even to quadrupeds. Allah Taalala has mentioned that, “They have got heart but do not feel, they have got eyes but do not see. They have got ears but do not hear; they are like quadruped animals, rather they are inferior to them. And It is they who are heedless”. (Sura: Al-Araf, Ayat: 179). From the discussion above, we can say that Jiku’s downfall is caused by the lack of proper moral education. And so his mother’s statement is correct in this regard.","image":null,"image_url":null}]

Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"The relationship of employer and employee should be like brothers. Man is a social being. No man on earth can do all his work alone. In this age of industrialization, every individual has to look up to others to sustain himself. One individual works under another at all levels of society, and one becomes an employer and the other his employee. As the employer cannot do without the help of the working class, so the working class is also dependent on the salary and allowance of the employer for their daily lives. That is why Islam does not approve any discrimination between the master and the worker in respect of every matter, including food, dress, etc. About the dignity and rights of the worker, Rasulullah (Sm) said, \"They (who work for you) are your brethren; Allah has made them subservient to you.\" (Bukhari and Muslim)","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Which aspect of Islam has been reflected in the behaviour and belief of Alal? Ibadat is an Arabic word, it means to express absolute humility and humbleness and to be extremely submissive. In the Islamic terminology, obedience to the regulations of Allah the Most High in all affairs of daily life is called Ibadat. Allah the Most High has created man for the purpose of worshipping Him. By Ibadat obedience and servitude to Allah is expressed, which is observed in the behaviour and belief of Alal. In the stem, the actions and belief of Alal indicate his attitude towards Ibadat. Because the purpose of creating humans is to worship Allah the Most High. The difference between man and other animals as creations of Allah is man’s intellect, conscience, and knowledge. If man fails to render servitude to Allah by applying his conscience, intellect, and knowledge, he becomes a peer of the quadrupeds or even inferior to them. Allah the Most High says, “They have got heart but do not feel, they have got eyes but do not see. They have got ears but do not hear; they are like quadruped animals, rather they are inferior to them. And it is they who are heedless.” (Sura: Al-Araf, Ayat: 179) Therefore, it can be said that the Ibadat of Allah the Most High is revealed in Alal’s behaviour and belief.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"Identify the Ibadat performed by Dulal and analyze its importance.","marks":4,"answer":"The Ibadat that Dulal performed is Salat. The significance of Salat in human life is immense. Salat is an Arabic word. Its meaning is supplication—to ask for forgiveness and to seek mercy. As a slave offers supplication, seeks mercy, and seeks pardon, so it is called Salat. The religious and societal importance of Salat is immense. It helps to attain nearness to Allah, Iman becomes firm, and the soul becomes purified. It also removes the difference between rich and poor, which is like the Ibadat performed by Dulal. The importance of Salat in a Muslim’s daily life is unlimited. Salat helps man attain the pleasure of Allah, the nearness of Allah, and the purification of the soul. The slave gets the company of his Lord. Salat makes man get up from bed early in the morning, which is very beneficial for their health. The Muslim gets the opportunity to assemble five times daily in a particular place. They can find out about each other’s situations. They can help one another in meal and woe. At this point, the social bond among them is boosted. Even so, there remains no distinction between rich and poor while standing in a row for Salat. As a result, there is equality among the Musallis. parts: [{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"What do you understand by the education?","marks":1,"answer":"Education is the application of the acquired knowledge and experience in one’s life.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"\"I have been sent as the teacher\" — Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"Our Prophet Hazrat Muhammad (Sm.) has introduced himself as teacher and therefore made that statement. He who imparts knowledge to us is our teacher. The Prophet Muhammad (Sm.) is the greatest teacher in our lives. He has enlightened humanity about Allah’s attributes, Allah’s Sifat, power, blessings, and other aspects. The Prophet (Sm.) has emphasized truth and beauty. He has forbidden the path of falsehood. Throughout his life, he practiced Allah’s decrees and provided us with practical education. The knowledge we have about personal life, society, nation, and economics, we have received from the Prophet. That is why he called himself a teacher.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Explain about the opinion of Mr. 'Ga' about the reason of the subsidence of the society and morality.","marks":3,"answer":"The opinion of Mr. ‘Ga’ regarding the downfall and moral degradation of the society is praiseworthy. Education is the backbone of a nation. Education helps humans become true humans and illuminates the human heart, dispelling ignorance with the light of knowledge. However, this education must include both Islamic and moral teachings. Mr. ‘Ga’ has expressed this matter in his words. Mr. ‘Ga’ states that the root cause of the decline in society and the degradation of morality in the present time is the lack of Islamic and ethical education. Islamic education, guided by the Quran and Hadith, is essential for shaping an individual who is honest, patriotic, responsible, and a good citizen. On the other hand, those who lack Islamic education remain unaware of Allah, the Hereafter, and the fear of Jahannam. Without a practical understanding of the consequences of all life’s actions, they may fall into various injustices. Islamic education instills morality in humans, elevating them above even animals. In this regard, Allah the Most Great said, “They have got heart but do not feel, they have got eyes but do not see. They have got ears but do not hear; they are like quadruped animals, rather they are inferior to them. And it is they who are heedless”. (Sura: Al-Araf, Ayat: 179).","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"Explain the last statement of Zahir Sir according to your text book.","marks":4,"answer":"According to the stem, the last statement given by Mr. Zahir sir is correct. The education system that encompasses Islam in its entirety and completeness is known as Islamic education. In other words, education that integrates the teachings of the Quran and Hadith is considered Islamic education. Through this education, the development of an individual’s morality is fostered. Therefore, moral education is an integral part of Islamic education. Zahir Sir’s last statement highlights this aspect. The last statement given by Zahir sir was that moral education is an inseparable part of Islamic education. The main purpose of Islamic education is to accept the rules of Allah and to achieve His satisfaction at all levels of life, starting from the personal life of a Muslim. The three fundamental aspects of Islamic education are Tawhid, Risalat, and Akhirat. These provide guidance for all aspects of human life, enabling individuals to choose the path of justice over injustice. By being aware of the consequences of actions in all spheres of life, they avoid wrongdoing. They do not engage in theft, lying, hooliganism, backbiting etc because they know the consequences for these sins. The Prophet Muhammad (Sm.) is the greatest teacher, sent to provide us with comprehensive moral education. He said, “I have been sent to bring noble moral qualities into perfection”. (Bukhari).It can be said from the above discussion that the Prophet (Sm.) has blossomed the moral sense of people through Islamic education. In summary, moral education is the integral part of Islamic education.","image":null,"image_url":null}]

He mainly wants to learn Ilm-i-Deeni because it refers to the knowledge regarding Islam. Such as- the knowledge of Al-Quran, Hadith, Fiqh, Tafsir etc. It is important to achieve Ilm-i-Deeni in human life. In this regard, Allah said, “Why a section of each group does not emerge well-equipped with the knowledge of religion so that they may warn their communities as they return to them (for advice)”. (Sura: At-Tauba, Ayat:122). So it can be said that it is important to achieve Ilm-i-Deen in human life and Fardin is interested in it.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"Though the subjects of aquiring knowledge of Fardin and Farjana are different, their purpose is the same and one. Give your opinion in favour of the statement.","marks":4,"answer":"Though the subjects of acquiring knowledge of Fardin and Farjana are different, their purpose is the same and one. I support this statement. Ilm is divided into two groups— (a) Ilm-i-Deeni (religious knowledge) and (b) Ilm-i-Duniya (mundane knowledge). Also Ilm can be divided into two categories— (1) Adorable Knowledge; (2) Avoidable knowledge. Adorable knowledge is that which brings good(welfare) both here and hereafter. These include the knowledge of morality, medical science, engineering, physics, chemistry etc. which are beneficial. Avoidable knowledge is that which does no good to mankind, rather causes harm both in this world and next life. Such as - immorality, theft, injustice etc. Both Fardin and Farjana, even though they acquire knowledge in different ways, both types of knowledge are valuable. Fardin is eager to gain religious knowledge, while his sister Farjana desires worldly knowledge. However, both of their intentions are to serve and work for the welfare of humanity. As per Islamic perspective, there is importance in acquiring religious education, just as there is importance in obtaining worldly education. However, it must not violate any of Allah's decrees. Ultimately, the purpose of Islam is to work for the well-being of humanity. Therefore, it can be said that both Fardin and Farjana acquiring knowledge for the betterment of humanity, even though the subjects of their knowledge are different.","image":null,"image_url":null}]

Our beloved prophet Hazrat Muhammad (Sm.) introduced himself (before mankind) as a teacher thus He said: \"I have not but been sent as a teacher.\" (Ibn Majah).","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"What type of Jihad is exposed in the character of Mr. Alim? Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"The behavior of Mr. Alim has indicated Jihad, which is the fight against his Nafs (his evil self). Jihad means labour, toil, effort, pain, trial, etc. And in the Islamic parlance, Jihad is to uphold Deen (Islam) and establishing truth and justice by the ways of sacrifice in terms of life, wealth etc. as through Ilm, good deeds, writing and speeches. Prophet Muhammad (Sm.) said, \"A true mujahid is he who struggles against his evil self (Nafs) in order to establish allegiance to Allah.\" (Musnad-i-Ahmad). Everything that is best, has Allah’s satisfaction. Jihad can only be for Allah’s satisfaction. Jihad is the fight to establish truth and justice and efforts, labor and perseverance for resisting all falsehood and injustice. Mr. Alim’s behavior reflected Jihad. In the stem, Mr. Alim tries his best to Obey Allah's order about Halal and Haram. If he ever violated anything, he brings himself back to the right path. Indeed, in all aspects of life, safeguarding the characteristics of faith and adhering to the rules and discipline of Islam are essential for a Mu’min. It is the duty of a Muslim to protect and uphold the Deen in every sphere of life. This includes maintaining the principles of Islam, ensuring its prosperity, and seeking Allah’s satisfaction. Additionally, when necessary, a Mu’min must engage in jihad to defend the Deen. Therefore, it is incumbent upon all of us to follow Allah’s prescribed guidelines, adhere to halal and haram, and lead our lives accordingly.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"\"As a result of Mr. Sabit's behaviour, both the employer and the employees will be benefited.\" — Present your arguments for this statement.","marks":4,"answer":"'Both the employer and the employees will be benefited from Mr. Sabit’s behaviour'— I agree with this statement. There is no difference between the employer and the employees in Islam. In Islam, the employees are treated as brothers. The relationship between employer and employees is very close. If an employer and a employee can establish a relationship within the path of Islam, then the employee will receive fair wages, and the employer will receive the rightful labor. They will coexist harmoniously in the workplace. Islam provides guidance on treating those under one’s authority with respect. Allah said, “Deal decently with your subordinates”. (Sura: Nisa, Ayat: 36). This behaviour is seen in Mr. Sabit. According to the stem, Mr. Sabit promptly pays the wages and benefits to his employees. He is also kind to his subordinates. Islam emphasizes such conduct with workers. The Prophet (Sm.) also said, “Pay the worker his dues before his sweat dries out.” (Ibn Majah) . Not delaying payment for labor is essential. The prophet (Sm.) said, “Do not employ him without fixing his pay”. The Prophet (Sm.) further stated, “When a slave (worker) performs his duties for his master nicely, and worships Allah properly, he gets double remuneration.” (Bukhari and Muslim). From the discussion above, we can say that all of us must follow the laws of labour as guided in Islam to ensure welfare of the nation and the state as well as the employee and employee both should fulfill their duties.","image":null,"image_url":null}]

Explain it.","marks":3,"answer":"The Ibadat performed by Julkarnine is Salat, which has immense social importance. Salat is an Arabic word. Its Persian synonym is Namaz. Its meaning is supplication, to ask for forgiveness and to seek mercy. As a slave offers supplication, seeks mercy and pardon, it is called Salat. Allah the Most Great has made Farz the five times daily Salat. MrAdil from the above stem offers five times Salat every day. Its religious and social importance is immense. The importance of Salat is unlimited in a Muslim's daily life. Salat helps attain nearness to Allah. The slave gets the company of Allah. Iman becomes firm, and the soul becomes purified. Even the importance of offering Salat in the congregation has been mentioned in many places in Al-Quran. The Muslims get the opportunity to assemble five times daily in a particular place. They can help one another in meal and woe. At this point, the social bond among them is boosted. Even when standing in a line, there is no distinction between rich and poor. As a result, equality develops among the Musallis (those who offer prayers). Man learns the lesson of working in unison by forgetting mutual differences of opinion by offering Salat. Salat inspires us about the importance of time, a sense of discipline, obedience to the leader, and leading a regulated and clean life. Hence, the religious and social importance of Salat is endless.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"Analyze the importance of the Ibadat mentioned in the table-B' according to the textbook.","marks":4,"answer":"The Ibadat performed by Julhas Miyan indicates Zakat, economic importance of which is unparallel. Zakat is the third of the five pillars of Islam. Allah the Most High has made provision of Zakat to bridge the gap between the rich and the poor. If a person has Nisab amount of wealth, Zakat is Farz on him. In the Islamic viewpoint, Zakat is not mercy of the rich to the poor, rather it is the right of the poor. Zakat is one of the sources of Islamic economic system. The economic foundation and the success of the social welfare projects are dependent on it. It moves forward the flow of wealth and it teaches to reduce the wastage of wealth. The wealth of the rich reaches the poor also instead of remaining concentrated. As a result, the state economy takes off. Production increases and unemployment is reduced. The insolvent section of population gradually becomes solvent. The economic base of the state becomes firm. Zakat produces fear of Allah in the mind of man. Unless a Muslim pays up Zakat, he cannot continue to remain a perfect Muslim. Allah says: “Those who do not pay up Zakat, and they are not believers in Akhirat too.” (Ha-min As-Sajdah, Ayat: 7) That is why it can be said that the chief guest presented the importance of Ibadat in the form of Zakat in his speech. They should definitely pay Zakat according to the Shariat, on whom Zakat is Farz.","image":null,"image_url":null}]

So, Mr. Nasir does an honest work to plant fruit tree. It is recorded as charity in the accounts Book of the grower for hereafter.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"Evaluate the result of Mr Jabir’s work in the light of Islam.","marks":4,"answer":"According to the stem, Mr. Jabir is an honest shopkeeper due to fair price and adulteration – free goods. Rasulullah (Sm.) said, \"A trustworthy, truthful businessman will be in the company of the martyrs on the Qiyamat Day.\" Allah the Most High has promised in Al-Quran paradise for them. However, for this, traders will have to fulfil two conditions. Firstly, they must conduct their business with honesty and truthfulness. Secondly, they must be faithful and trustworthy. parts: [{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"What is \"Shan-i-Nuzul\"?","marks":0,"answer":"The cause or background of the revelation of the Sura or Ayat of Al-Quran is called 'Shan-i-Nuzul'.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"\"Recite the Quran slowly and clearly.\" — Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"Allah Ta’ala has revealed the mentioned verse by instructions to recite the Quran with Tazbid. Al-Quran should be studied with understanding, reflection,and research. Alongside reflection and research, it is very necessary to read the Quran correctly and nicely. An incorrect and unimpressive recitation of Al-Quran brings sin with it. The method of correct and nice recitation of Al-Quran is termed as Tazbid. Allah Ta’ala said about recitation of Quran with Tazbid, \"Recite the Quran slowly and clearly\" (Sura Al-Muzammil, Ayat 4).","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"What type of Sura did Mr. Sadik recite? Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"Mr. Sadik has recited the Madani Surahs of Al-Quran. Al-Quran is divided into 30 parts in total. There are 114 suras in Al-Quran. Considering the time of revelation, the suras of Al-Quran are divided into 2 groups. Such as- Makki and Madani. The suras revealed in Madinah are the Madani Suras. In Madani suras the principles of worshipping Allah, Salat, Sawm, Zakat, Haji, rules and regulations of Shariat, Farz, Wajib etc. are clearly mentioned. It is similar to the recited suras by Mr. Sadiq. In the stem it is mentioned that Mr. Sadiq recites some suras after waking up in the morning where a discussion related to the regulations of Salat, Zakat, and Haji are mentioned. Here, mainly Madani suras are being mentioned. In these suras the principles of Ibadat, Salat, Zakat, Haji, Sawm etc. have been described. The rules and regulations of Shariat, Farz, Wajib, etc. are clearly mentioned in them. Besides, introduction of Nifaq and conspiracies of the Munafiqs are mentioned. Personal, domestic, social, national, internal, educational and cultural principles have been described in these suras. The laws and regulations in respect of family transactions, inheritance, commerce and business, buying and selling and such other economic activities are described as well. Judicial matters, penal code, Jihad, code of laws, diplomatic policy etc. have been discussed in them. That is why it can be said that the suras that Mr. Sadik has recited are the Madani suras.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"Evaluate the advice of Mr. Sadik in the light of the relevant Sura of text book.","marks":4,"answer":"The advice of Mr.Sadik to his son is proper in the light of Sura Ad-Duha. Sura Ad-Duha is the 93rd Sura of Al-Quran. In this Sura Allah the Most High has narrated numerous favours given to the Holy Prophet Hazrat Muhammad (Sm). Again, He also commands Rasul (Sm) to express his gratitude. The teachings of this Sura is reflected in the stem. In the stem the advice given by Mr. Sadik to his elder son is proper in the light of Sura Ad-Duha. Because, we get this lesson from Sura Ad-Duha. Here, it is told that Allah saves His dear slaves from danger and calamities, He grants them blissful life. Besides, He provides them many blessings. For this, as the gratitude for these blessings, rich and solvent persons should help and cooperate with poor, needy, orphan and beggars as much as possible. They should not be harsh towards needy and orphans asking for help, they should not be scolded or beaten rather good behaviour should be done with them. Lastly, it can be said that, Mr. Sadik has provided correct advice to his son in the light of Sura Ad-Duha. And all of us should implement the teachings of Sura Ad-Duha in our life.","image":null,"image_url":null}]

Allah the Most High says about this, \"Indeed it is the holy Quran which has been inscribed on the protected plate.\" (Sura: Al-Buruj, Ayats 21-22). The complete code of life and direction for all men to come till the Qiyamat are available in Al-Quran. So, its preservation is necessary. Allah the Most Great has assumed the responsibility of its protection. He announces thus, \"It is we who have revealed the Quran and surely we are its protector.\" (Sura: Al-Hijr, Ayat: 9).","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Which Sura's teaching is manifested in scenario-1? Explain it.","marks":3,"answer":"The teaching of Sura At-Tin is manifested in scenario-1. Sura At-Tin is the 95th Sura of Al-Quran. In this Sura, human are declared as the best and most beautiful among all creations. In this Sura, Allah has described about the shape and nature of human which is expressed in scenario-1. In scenario-1, Miss Rahela Omar was chosen as the first Hijab Miss World-2022 considering body structure, size, shape, personality etc. This incident of scenario-1 reflects the beautiful shape and creation of human described in Sura At-Tin. The teaching of this sura is that though human are the most beautiful creation of world, if they do not perform good deeds, they will be held accountable by Allah in earth and Akhirai and will be punished severely. So, everyone should not show pride and perform all principles of Islam properly.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"Do you think that the activities of Mr. Sobur's wife shown in scenario-2 are accurate? Evaluate it in the light of your text book.","marks":4,"answer":"No, the activities of Mr. Sobur’s wife shown in scenario-2 are not accurate in the light of Sura Al-Maun. Sura Al-Maun is the 107th sura of Al-Quran. Allah Ta’ala has described some characteristics of Munafiqs in this sura. Among these, two special features of Munafiqs are that they are indifferent to Salat and they do not give small household objects to others. In the activities of Mr. Sobur’s wife, one of these characteristics can be observed. Mr. Sobur’s wife, mentioned in scenario-2, provides small household objects to her neighbours which is an activity worth praising. But, she is inattentive towards her prayers which is similar to the characteristics of Munafiq. Because, Munafiqs are inattentive towards Salat. Sometimes, they offer prayer to show others. And for Salat performed by such class awaits sufferings and severe punishment. So, it can be said that, Mr. Sobur’s wife need to be careful in offering prayers according to the teaching of Sura Al-Maun. Rather than offering prayer for showing others and inattentively, she will have to pray with faithfulness and sincerity.","image":null,"image_url":null}]

Allah the Most High has narrated the various commands and prohibitions, rules and regulations and the principles of Shariah in the Quran briefly. Rasulullah (Sm) would impart the necessary explanation of rules and regulations of Al-Quran. In most cases he would teach them practically by practicing them himself. It is these sayings and deeds of Rasulullah (Sm) that are called Hadith. Therefore, for following the rules and regulations of Al-Quran clearly, the importance of Hadith is immense.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Implementation of which Hadith has been reflected in the activities of Mr. Rafee? Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"In the activities of Mr. Rafee, the implementation of Hadith related to plantation is noticed. Tree plantation is an act of merit. It is said in a Hadith about this, \"If a Muslim plants a sapling (tree) or grows any crop, and if some birds, men or animals eat a portion from that, then it will be counted as charity on his behalf.\" (Bukhari and Muslim) This Hadith encourages us in tree plantation. Man can get benefitted in many ways through trees. Man can earn benefit through this in the next life parallel with benefits in this life. The implementation of this Hadith is noticeable in the activities of Mr. Rafee. Mr. Rafee's thinking and activities are possible because of Hadith related to plantation. And, in the eye of Islam, his such activity can be termed as charity. Because, in Hadith, it is said, If a Muslim plants a sapling (tree) or grows any crop, it can be a reason of charity. Because, birds, animals, worms and insects feed on crops and fruits. For this, the planters and farmers get rewards. Allah the Most High gets this reward recorded in his accounts-book to the same tune as he could earn by giving that crop in charity. Thus, it can be said that, the real example of Hadith related to tree plantation exists in the activities of Mr. Rafee.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"Determine the validity of the comment of uncle in regard of Safee's activities, in the light of relevant Hadith.","marks":4,"answer":"The comment of Safee's uncle in regard of his activities is valid in the light of Hadith on philanthropy and service to the created beings of the textbook. Allah the Most High is the creator of everything. Except Himself, all the rest that exist are creations or makhluq. As man is His creation, so are the insects and worms. Having mercy towards these makhluq is service to the created beings. In Safee's activity, this service is expressed. The comment of Safee's uncle is correct. Because, Allah the Most High has created everything of this universe. He is the Nourisher, Cherisher, Sustainer and Controller of everything. But, He has not created all things in an identical mould. This is a test taken by Him. He has divided the creations in various groups and species, and maintains all for the benefit of mankind. So, man should behave well with all the creations. The Holy Prophet (Sm) said, \"All created beings constitute the Family of Allah. So, the dearest to Allah is that man who favours His created beings most.\" (Baihaqi). Allah the Most High becomes pleased if kindness is shown to His creatures and loves them more. From the above discussions, it can be understood that the work of Safee is included in service to the created beings. And the comment of his uncle regarding this is also valid. Through this activity, Safee will be able to gain more love from Allah the Most High.","image":null,"image_url":null}]

Allah proclaims to have created man in the best of shapes. The shape of man is the most excellent among all created things and beings. The marks of Munafiq has come out by the activities of Sajib. To be inattentive in Salat, not to perform Salat in time etc. are behaviour of a Munafiq. parts: [{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"What do you understand by Haram?","marks":1,"answer":"The actions or things which are abominable and therefore, rejectable and discardable in pursuance of the clear directions of Al-Quran and Sunnah, are Haram.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"\"Farz-i-Kifaya\" is the combined Farz —Make it clear.","marks":2,"answer":"Farz-i-Kifaya is collective Farz. The duties that are Farz on Muslims, but if performed by a group of Muslims in the society, it will be accepted on behalf of all Muslims. The rest non performing Muslims are exempted from this obligation due to its performance by a group of Muslims. But, if any group does not perform it, all members of that society will be sinners. For example, the Janaza Salat (funeral prayer for a Muslim) etc.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Evaluate the act of 'Y'.","marks":3,"answer":"The act of Mr. 'Y' will be counted as Sadaq-e-Zariya. Plantation and agriculture are very essential for human life. Man derives much benefit from this. Prophet (Sm) said about this in Hadith, \"If a Muslim plants a sapling (tree) or grows any crop, and if some birds, men or animals eat a portion from that, then it will be counted as charity on his behalf.\" (Bukhari and Muslim) There is similarity of the description of this Hadith with the act of 'Y'. Mr 'Y' plants trees every year beside the road of his village taking lessons from a Hadith of Prophet (Sm). The activities of 'Y' are relatable to the Hadith discussed above. That is why, this act of him is termed as Sadaq (charity) in the language of Hadith. Man can earn benefit from plantation in the next life parallel with benefits in this life. For, birds, animals, worms and insects feed on crops and fruits. For this the planters and farmers get rewards. Allah the Most High gets this reward recorded in his account book to the same tune as he could earn by giving that crop in charity. As a result, he owns much reward even without himself being aware of that.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"Mention the teaching of the Hadith that has been violated by Saimun regarding the business, then justify the citation of Mr. Imam.","marks":4,"answer":"Saimun violated the teaching of honesty in business that is indicated in Hadith. And the citation of Mr. Imam regarding this is correct. Businessman Saimun adulterates with good commodities by the bad ones in his shop and sales in high price. But, the Holy Prophet (Sm) has imposed two conditions in case of business. Firstly, the business must be conducted with honesty and truthfulness. Secondly, the businessmen must be faithful and trustworthy. That is, business and trade will have to be conducted with honesty and faithfulness. Men provide less in weigh being owned by greed, sells bad commodity by calling them good. They adulterate bad commodity with good ones, hide the problems in the commodity. They do many unethical works like hoarding. Saimun's activity is opposite to these conditions. The Imam's citation is from the Hadith: \"A trustworthy, truthful businessman will be in the company of the martyrs on the Qiyamat Day.\" This Hadith promises great reward for honest traders. Since Saimun violates the condition of honesty, he will not get this reward. The Imam's statement is thus a reminder of the correct Islamic business ethic.","image":null,"image_url":null}]

parts: [{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"What is called Sunnat-i-Zaida?","marks":1,"answer":"Those acts which are proved to have been performed by the Holy Prophet (Sm) but not always; rather, which he would do at one time but did not do at other times, are called the Sunnat-i-Zaida.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"Explain the importance of Ijma.","marks":2,"answer":"The importance and necessity of Ijma in Islamic Shariat is immense. The origin of Ijma has been noticeable from the time of Rasul (Sm). Rasulullah (Sm) himself would seek advice of his companions on various issues. Allah the Most High says: “And their affairs are resolved on the basis of mutual consultation.” (Sura: Sura, Ayat, 38). In this way, Rasulullah (Sm) settle legitimacy, example and ideal of Ijma. If proper solution of any matter is not found in Quran and Hadith, for combined decision of the Mujtahids of Muslim Ummah, necessity of Ijma until Qiyamat is immense.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"The activities of Mr. ‘Ka’ is opposite of the teaching of which Hadith? Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"The activities of Mr. ‘Ka’ is opposite of the teachings of Hadith related to Niyyat or motive. The purpose or aim of the deed is called Niyyat. People will get the outcome of their doings according to their Niyyat. In the Hadith related to Niyyat, Prophet (Sm) said, “In fact, all deeds (their results) are dependent on intention” (Bukhari). In the activities of Mr. ‘Ka’, opposite of this Hadith can be seen. Mr. ‘Ka’ of the stem went for Haji but his intention was to buy pure gold by cheap rate. In such activities of Mr. ‘Ka’, he will not get any blessing, because his Niyyat is not right. The teaching of the Hadith related to Niyyat is Alongside the outward deed, Allah the Most High notices the state of the mind too. Thus, if anyone does good work in bad motive, he will still not get any blessing. That is why the precondition of any work is the purity of Niyyat. But, it is absent in the activities of Mr.‘Ka’. Hence, his work is opposite to the Hadith related to Niyyat.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"Evaluate the Sumon’s activities after identifying the opinion of Mr. ‘Kha’ is opposite of the teaching of which Sura.","marks":4,"answer":"The opinion of Mr. ‘Kha’ is against the teachings of Sura Al-Maun. Sura Al-Maun is the 107th Sura of Al-Quran. In the third Ayat of this Sura, Allah said by presenting the characteristics of Munafiqs, “And does not encourage offering food to the needy”. Through this ayat, Allah has made us alert about nifaq, and ordered us to stay away from this characteristics. But, in the comment of Mr. ‘Kha’, opposite characteristics of this has been expressed. In the stem, Sumon, friend of Mr. ‘Kha’, arranges food for orphans and destitutes by the favour of government job. At this ‘Kha’ told by commenting negatively, you have got this job by your own intellect. So, why will you feed others? Such comment of ‘Kha’ is not acceptable at all. Because, Allah has ordered regarding feeding orphans and destitutes. And those who do not help the orphans and needles despite having ability and discourage others regarding this, will be counted as Munafiq. On the other hand, by arranging food for orphans and needy, Sunnan has fulfilled the responsibility of Iman. So, it can be said that, for discouraging in the works of orphan and needy, Mr. ‘Kha’ is a Munafiq. And for this, he will have to face punishment in the life after death.","image":null,"image_url":null}]

parts: [{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"What is Nazira Tilawat?","marks":1,"answer":"The visual recitation of Al-Quran is called Nazira Tilawat.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"Why is Islam called a dynamic code of life?","marks":2,"answer":"Islam is called a dynamic code of life because there is specific instruction in Islam about new problems of the continuously changeable society. Islam is the religion or code of life provided by Allah the Most High. This is a complete code of life. The direction of all the problems of human life is provided in this. The laws of solving newly originated problems of the society changing with time are available in Islam. If the solution of any newly originated problem is not found directly in Al-Quran and Hadith, then the problem can be solved by according to Jima and Qiyas. For these reasons, Islam is called a dynamic code of life.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Which Hadith's teachings are reflected in the character of Mr. Amin? Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"The teachings of the Hadith related to Patience and Forbearance is reflected in the behaviour of Mr. Amin. Prophet (Sm) said about patience and forbearance, \"A Mumin's every deed is amazing. And each deed brings him well being and good. And none but a Mumin can get it. When he enjoys happiness and peace, he expresses gratitude. It is good for him. And if he suffers sorrows and pain, he adopts patience. This too is good for him.\" (Muslim). The teaching of this Hadith is expressed in the behaviour of Mr. Amin. Mr. Amin of the stem is a fish farmer. His fish farm has swept away by flood water. As a result, he suffered a lot financially. But, he has not been disappointed. Rather he has started working in a new zeal by depending on Allah. From this incident, it can be understood that, Mr. Amin has taken lesson from the Hadith related to patience and forbearance. Because, this Hadith teaches that both happiness and sorrow is beneficial for Mumin. That is why, one must not despair at the time of sorrow and pains. Rather, one must obey the commands of Allah with patience.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"Justify the statement of the Islamic scholar in light of the related Hadith of your textbook.","marks":4,"answer":"The statement of the Islamic scholar about honest businessman Mr. Helal is accurate in the light of the Hadith related to honesty in business. Business and commerce are a noble profession. Our beloved Prophet (Sm) too was a businessman. An honest and trustworthy businessman commands high esteem both here and the hereafter. Mr. Helal is also an honest businessman. He will also gain this esteem. Mr. Helal of the stem is a big businessman. He does not adulterate the products despite having the opportunity. He sells the products in fair price. Knowing about him, an Islamic scholar said, \"This type of businessman will get great reward in the day of Qiyamat\". Here, the Islamic scholar talked about the prize set for honest businessman. Because, in the day of Qiyamat, the trustworthy and truthful businessmen will become companions of the martyrs. Rasulullah (Sm) has said about this, \"A trustworthy, truthful businessman will be in the company of the martyrs on the Qiyamat Day\". (Ibn Majah) After the above discussion, it can be said that Mr. Helal is an honest businessman. The statement of the Islamic scholar about reward of honest businessman on the day of Qiyamat is correct. That is why, all of us should try to be trustworthy and truthful in business.","image":null,"image_url":null}]
